concepts.title: Radius and tangent
concepts.explanation: The radius to the point of contact is perpendicular to a tangent. Centre, contact point and an external point form a right triangle.

example.problem: PA is tangent at A, O is the centre and ∠OPA = 40°. Find ∠AOP in degrees.

concepts.commonMistake: The radius must end at the point of contact for the perpendicular rule.
checklist: Use triangle angle sums or Pythagoras.

concepts.title: Equal tangent segments
concepts.explanation: Two tangent segments from the same external point to the same circle have equal lengths. Shared external points allow equal segments to be paired in larger figures.

example.problem: PA and PB are tangents from P to one circle. PA = 2x + 2 and PB = 10 cm. Find x.

concepts.commonMistake: Tangents from different external points need not have equal lengths.

concepts.title: Number of tangents
concepts.explanation: A point inside a circle has no tangent through it, a point on it has one, and an external point has two. Compare its centre-distance with the radius.

example.problem: OP = 6 cm for a circle of radius 6 cm. How many tangents pass through P?
steps: P lies on the circle, where there is exactly one tangent.

concepts.commonMistake: A line through an interior point cuts the circle, so it is not a tangent.

concepts.title: Finding tangent lengths
concepts.explanation: In right triangle OAP, OA is radius r, OP is centre-distance d, and PA = √(d² − r²). OP is the hypotenuse.

example.problem: PA is a tangent of length 24 cm; the circle radius is 10 cm. Find OP in cm.

concepts.commonMistake: Do not subtract lengths before squaring, or mistake the radius for the hypotenuse.

concepts.title: Angles between tangents
concepts.explanation: For tangents PA and PB, the smaller angle APB and smaller central angle AOB sum to 180°. OP also bisects the angle between the tangent segments.

example.problem: Tangents PA and PB form angle 40°. O is the centre. Find ∠APO in degrees.
steps: OP bisects the angle between the tangent segments.

concepts.commonMistake: The two right angles occur at the contact points, not at P or O.
checklist: Use the angle bisector only with the shared centre and point.

questions.prompt: A convex quadrilateral ABCD has a circle tangent to all four sides. AB = 6, BC = 8, CD = 10 cm. Find DA in cm.
questions.explanation: Equal tangent segments give AB + CD = BC + DA. DA = 6 + 10 − 8 = 8.

questions.prompt: A convex quadrilateral ABCD has a circle tangent to all four sides. AB = 9, BC = 12, CD = 15 cm. Find DA in cm.
